subject: Insurance deliverables & endorsement alignment for MSA + Order Form

From: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@acme.com>

Subject: Insurance deliverables for MSA + Order Form

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the updated MSA and draft order form. Procurement and Legal at ACME need the insurance evidence checklist to close the PO. Can you confirm what Redwood will provide at signature vs. post-signature? Specifically:

- COI (ACORD 25) naming ACME as certificate holder and PO number on the certificate
- Additional Insured endorsement (we typically ask for ISO CG 20 10 or equivalent)
- Primary & non-contributory wording and waiver of subrogation
- Carrier NAIC and policy period matching the effective date

We can accept an endorsement PDF from the carrier or a broker-signed letter if the carrier cannot produce the endorsement immediately. Also attaching ACME's certificate template for formatting.

Can you loop in legal on what Redwood can commit to pre- and post-execution? We are aiming to get everything in place within 5 business days of order execution.

Thanks,
Emily Shaw
Senior Procurement Manager
ACME Corp

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Insurance deliverables for MSA + Order Form (tracked asks)

Hi Emily / team —

Thanks — I reviewed the ACME template and Aditya's note. Below are the specific insurance commitments Redwood can make in the Order Form and the items where we need a short exception process. I attached a suggested endorsement PDF (Redwood_Endorsement_Suggestion) and a tracked redline of the MSA.

Committed (we can add these to the Order Form):
- General Liability: $2M per occurrence / $4M aggregate (we will list limits in the order form)
- Commercial Auto & Employers Liability: limits as stated in the MSA
- Cyber / E&O: $5M aggregate
- COI (ACORD 25) naming "ACME Corp / PO {PO_NUMBER}" as Certificate Holder — delivered at or before execution where broker permits

Endorsement & wording (post-signature delivery window: 5 business days):
- Additional Insured: Redwood will procure an endorsement granting ACME additional insured status for liabilities arising out of Redwood's performance under the Order Form. Preferred language: ISO CG 20 10 (or carrier equivalent) limited to the scope of the Order Form.
- Primary & Non-Contributory: Redwood will request primary and non-contributory wording from carriers; we will provide carrier confirmation or the endorsement when available. Note: some carriers restrict full non-contributory language when a significant self-insured retention applies — we can escalate for exceptions.
- Waiver of Subrogation: Redwood will seek waiver of subrogation in favor of ACME where permitted by policy. If carrier refusal, we will provide a broker attestation explaining the restriction.
- Cancellation/Notice: Standard 30 days notice for non-payment/90 days for policy cancellation; we will confirm exact notice language in the endorsement.

Open items / exceptions process:
- If ACME requires boilerplate-only endorsement (e.g., an explicit ISO form without equivalency language), we need to confirm whether an endorsement equivalent from the carrier is acceptable.
- If ACME requires naming additional parties or affiliates beyond the PO/ACME umbrella, that will require review and potential amendment to limits.

Please confirm that the endorsement equivalency is acceptable and whether ACME requires the ISO form itself or will accept carrier-letter/broker-letter evidence while the endorsement follows. Once confirmed, Aditya and I will finalize the Order Form clause and provide the ACORD template and endorsement PDF for your broker.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Legal Ops (ACME Corp) <legal-ops@acme.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com, b.jensen@jensenbrokers.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Insurance deliverables for MSA + Order Form — endorsement acceptability

Lauren / Aditya —

Thanks for the breakdown. A couple quick points from ACME Legal:

1) Primary & Non-contributory — ACME's standard position is that the additional insured endorsement must be primary and non-contributory. We understand carrier limitations, but request that Redwood obtain an endorsement phrased as primary & non-contributory to the maximum extent permitted by law/policy, and include a broker letter if the carrier cannot provide it.

2) ISO form — our preference is to see the ISO CG 20 10 (or the exact equivalent) where possible. If your carrier provides an "equivalent" endorsement, please include carrier language and broker attestation explaining the equivalency for our records.

3) Waiver of Subrogation — ACME will accept a waiver where the policy permits. If there is a SEL (self-insured retention) or other restriction, include a short explanation in the broker letter.

4) Timing — 5 business days post-execution for the endorsement is acceptable. For the COI, we require the ACORD to be uploaded on the execution day with PO number populated.

Please provide the ACORD 25 with the certificate holder exactly as: "ACME Corp — Accounts Payable / PO {PO_NUMBER}" and the endorsement or broker letter as separate PDF attachments. Also include the insurer NAIC number and contact for audit verification.

If you can produce the broker contact and a provisional timeline by EOD Monday (4 Oct), we can clear procurement hold for signature.

Regards,
Legal Ops (ACME Corp)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
